component.name: Kase
component.summary: AirPods battery, controls and island overlay for Linux

description.p: Kase is a zero-configuration AirPods companion for Linux desktops, at its best on KDE Plasma. It finds your earbuds on its own, starts with your session and stays out of the way in the system tray.

ul.li: Accurate left, right and case battery levels, including charging state
An island overlay in the manner of the iPhone's Dynamic Island, with battery for each earbud and the case and short alerts for charging, low battery and noise control
Noise control mode switching: noise cancellation, transparency and adaptive
Ear detection: pauses and resumes your media when you take an earbud out
Conversational awareness: lowers the volume while you speak
Keeps audio working when the earbuds go out of range and come back

description.p: The overlay is a normal desktop surface and never touches game processes, so it is safe to use with anti-cheat protected games.
Kase is built on LibrePods, the open AirPods protocol project, and shares its AGPL-3.0 licence.
Kase is not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc. AirPods is a trademark of Apple Inc.

description.p: Clearer wording for the battery setting: it is now called Quicker battery updates when not connected, with a plain explanation of what it does.
Faster battery while away, one switch away.

ul.li: A new switch in Settings, Diagnostics turns on Bluetooth's experimental features so case and pod levels update sooner while the AirPods aren't connected
Works across distributions like Apple device mode, and the two switches stay independent
ARM64 bundles for the Raspberry Pi 5, Asahi Linux and ARM laptops
The installer picks the right bundle for your PC by itself

description.p: AirPods for Linux: Kase now feels at home on every major distribution and desktop.

ul.li: One install command for Fedora, Bazzite, SteamOS, Ubuntu, Debian, Arch, openSUSE and NixOS
The island turns see-through over fullscreen games on Plasma 5, Sway, Hyprland and niri
Works with PulseAudio as well as PipeWire, and knows many more call and effects apps
Uses the Bluetooth adapter your AirPods are paired on, on PCs with two adapters
A Diagnostics section in Settings shows what your system supports

description.p: Your PC is home: the AirPods come back to it by themselves, and reconnect after a day away.

ul.li: The AirPods return to the PC a few seconds after your iPhone stops playing (can be turned off in Settings)
A phone notification no longer keeps the AirPods while you game or sit in a Discord call
Reconnects after a day out with your iPhone, and as soon as you unlock the PC
A tidier, faster codebase, and settings that survive a power cut
A log file that explains every switching decision

description.p: BazzitePods is now Kase: AirPods for KDE Plasma.

ul.li: New name and app id; updating with the install command moves your settings and saved AirPods across
The old BazzitePods app and its autostart entry are removed for you
No other changes: same features, same settings

description.p: A purist Dynamic Island, a redesigned app window, one-click Apple device mode, and a mic switch that works on AirPods 4.

ul.li: Purist style, now the default: solid flat black with a hairline edge, like the iPhone's Dynamic Island
Light runs round the border in the event's colour when something happens, then the island rests
Small, Medium, Large and Extra large island sizes
Redesigned app window: pure black, three tabs, and a preview screen for placing the overlay
Apple device mode is one switch in Settings: confirm, enter your password, done
Holding the left stem swaps the mic on AirPods 4, with a soft chime telling you which mic you're on
The AirPods mic sends sound, and every app moves with the swap, including Discord and EasyEffects

description.p: Use the AirPods as the PC's mic while music stays in full quality.

ul.li: Hold the left stem to swap between your desk mic and the AirPods mic (turn on "AirPods mic switch" first)
Hold the right stem to change noise control
Apps follow the swap, and the PC returns to the desk mic when the AirPods go to another device or a call starts
The overlay shows which mic is in use

description.p: AirPods come back when you do.

ul.li: AirPods that left with you reconnect when you come home, however long you were away
AirPods you disconnect on this PC stay disconnected

description.p: More of your AirPods, and clearer battery when they are away from the PC.

ul.li: New settings read from the AirPods: automatic ear detection, Adaptive Audio strength, noise cancellation with one AirPod, microphone choice and automatic connection
Charging and live levels show while the AirPods are nearby but not connected
Says "In case" when both pods are put away, with a hint to open the lid to update the case
Personalized Volume shows the AirPods' real setting

description.p: The overlay becomes an island, modelled on the iPhone's Dynamic Island.

ul.li: Opens into a card with a ring for each pod and the case, and rests as a slim island
Short alerts for charging, low battery, noise control changes, switching to and from an iPhone, and disconnecting
Spring animations, cross-fading contents, sweeping rings and rolling numbers
Sits at the top center by default; Glass at 0% is the island's pure black
Redraws only while it moves and uses no CPU at rest

description.p: Reliable switching with an iPhone for every app, with overlay feedback.

ul.li: The AirPods return to the PC about a second after playback starts in apps that do not report playback to the system, such as the Plex desktop app
Idle voice-chat streams, audio effects and notification sounds no longer count as playback
The overlay shows which device has the AirPods and when they are back on the PC
Phone calls on the iPhone are never interrupted

description.p: Faster, more reliable switching between an iPhone and the PC.

ul.li: The PC takes the AirPods back about a second after playback starts
iPhone notifications no longer take the AirPods while the PC is playing
Short status messages from the iPhone no longer pause playback on the PC

description.p: First release of Kase as its own app.

ul.li: New app id, icon and Flatpak with a minimal set of permissions
Starts automatically with your session, minimized to the tray
More accurate battery readings for each earbud and the case
On-screen battery overlay
Audio keeps working after the earbuds reconnect
